channel.title: What is the first scp?
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "What is the first scp?" - I'm not talking about SCP-173, I mean the first SCP the foundation has contained.

item.title: Maybe it is 173
item.content:encoded:
Even though 173 was first written, I mean the SCP that was the first one that was discovered

Besides the numerical designation, is there any proof that 173 wasn't the first SCP discovered, he was moved to Site-19 in like, the 80s or 90s, meaning he was in Site/Area-[REDACTED] for quite some time, possibly even longer than his stay at site 19. Honestly though, jokes aside it's a safe bet that 002 was the first DISCOVERED by the foundation, however like someone else said if you take his claims of being 'god' at face value (which I don't) he would be the first SCP. By the way in my personal opinion 343 is just a powerful reality bender who is also good at acting.

item.title: Re: What is the first scp?
item.content:encoded:
The Database. I mean,

Major spoilers for The Database
Spoiled

The Database's idea is that SCP-001 is us, the horror writers. Every author is older than 14 years, which is the age of SCP-173, the second SCP. Now, this is very meta and you might not understand. But we are the oldest SCP.

item.title: Re: What is the first scp?
item.content:encoded: I remember when I first saw that and loved it. I'm glad you reminded me it existed.

item.title: Re: What is the first scp?
item.content:encoded:
Since I always favor silliness, I say it's Thing-I-U.

And despite being from a joke skip, this one actually make sense in universe.

item.title: Re: What is the first scp?
item.content:encoded:
Seems reasonable. And I could definitely have been thinking of any number of things.
Although, it did play into an idea that started in my brain-meat at work about a potential 001 being such an 'inherited' SCP from a Parent or Grandparent organization.

"The Bound Titan"
Prometheus himself is SCP-001

Or, for something more ominous

The pieces of Uranus that Chronos scattered across the world when he cut him apart to seize the throne of the Titans. (Just imagine what an immortal hunk of Titan, constantly regrowing injured tissue can do to other things when the worms that consume said tissue metamorphose into dragons, after all)

item.title: Re: What is the first scp?
item.content:encoded:
I seem to recall at least one article asserting that the Foundation was formed by a merger of several smaller Occult organizations into one.

You're probably recalling the Wrong Proposal, although the Foundation being formed from a predecessor organization (whether that be the ASCI or some combination of occult groups) is a part of site mythology, frankly. It's either that or a group of Western elites banding together to create the first 05 Council. That's usually how it goes, anyways.

item.title: Re: What is the first scp?
item.content:encoded:
I seem to recall at least one article asserting that the Foundation was formed by a merger of several smaller Occult organizations into one.
Likely they all had their own collections at the time of the merger, if we accept this idea. So, whatever the oldest such object was is probably the "First" SCP.

If you accept 343's claims at face value, being "God" IT would probably be the "first" SCP, or at least the first anomaly.

item.title: Re: What is the first scp?
item.content:encoded:
If it isn't one of those 001 then it likely to be 001-ex, natural number start with 1 after all.

Ok, maybe the Foundation has several objects in its founding days and thus didn't register it with 001. That's possible too. And with our no-canon policy, it can be anything.

item.title: What is the first scp?
item.content:encoded: Even though 173 was the first written, I mean the first SCP that the first one that was discovered (excluding 001 proposals)
